title: Simple Analytics Reading
summary: Views alone can be misleading — check Watch Time, Save Rate, and Action Metric weekly.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Introduction
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **Views alone are not enough**.
- **The number of views might make you happy** — **but it doesn't tell the whole truth**. **Posts with fewer views** **can have a much greater impact**.
- **What's important** **is to understand the right signals:** **what indicates** **that the content is building an audience** **rather than just passing through the feed**.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: The Problem
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Focusing on a single number** **can mislead you**.
- **When all your decisions are based on views** — **you might repeat a type of content** **that brings traffic** **without trust or conversion**.
- **You feel like you are working hard** **but real growth is slow** — **because you are measuring something** **that is not related to your main goal**.

sections.heading: Core Idea
sections.subtitle: Read the Post with Three Signals
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Focus on 3 indicators:** **Watch Time**, **Save Rate**, **Follow/Action Rate** — **Action Metric**.
- **Watch Time** **indicates if the start was engaging**. **Save Rate** **shows if the value is worth returning**. **Action Metric** **indicates if trust has increased**.
- **Every week**, **review the last 3 posts** — **and write down just one improvement decision**. **Regular small improvements** **are better than random large changes**.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Superficial Reading or Smart Reading?
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Superficial Reading | Smart Reading |
|--------------------|---------------|
| **A post that got high views is great** — **without understanding Watch Time and Save Rate** | **I review 3 key indicators before judging** — **I know what to repeat** **for long-term growth** |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Simple Analytics Terms
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|--------|---------|
| **Watch Time** | **Average time** **that people completed the content** | **If the start is weak** **you will see the number drop quickly** |
| **Save Rate** | **The save rate** **compared to the number of views** | **The more practical the value** **the higher the save rate tends to be** |
| **Action Metric** | **An indicator of a real action** **after viewing** | **A post with fewer views** **but got serious messages = a stronger metric** |

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick Confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 1

**Question:** **You have two posts:** **the first has higher views but a weak Save Rate** — **and the second has fewer views but better Watch Time and Save**. **Which one do you rely on** **as a signal to improve the next content?**

the first** **because it has higher views**.**
**the second** **because it is stronger in quality and intent**.
neither** — **I choose based on mood**.**

**Explanation:** **The indicators that reflect true value** **are more important than the raw view number** — **because they lead to stronger growth**.
bullets: the first** **because it has higher views**.**
**the second** **because it is stronger in quality and intent**.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: Identify the Most Important Metric for Each Post
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** **Choose 3 posts** — **decide on the most important metric** **that truly reflects its success**.

**Submission:** For each post — goal · most important metric · reason · **one decision for next week**

**Evaluation Criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Metric Selection | 50% | **Each post has a clear and justified metric** — **no general selection** |
| Executive Decision | 50% | **One improvement decision** **directly related to the analysis** |
